info.name: Skandha Transcoder API
info.description:
# Skandha Transcoder — control-plane API

FastAPI control plane in front of a C++/GStreamer engine. Folders `01`–`09` are the **reference**: one request per endpoint. Folders `W0`–`W6` are **runnable workflows** — open the Collection Runner, pick a `W` folder, set **Delay = 1000 ms**, and hit Run.

## Start here

`W0 Smoke test` — read-only, five assertions, proves the container is healthy.

## No authentication

There is none. Use only on a trusted management network.

## Three rules this API enforces

**1. Optimistic concurrency.** Queue mutations carry `expectedRevision`; rundown mutations carry `expectedVersionId`. Read it with a GET first — a stale value is `409`.

**2. Asynchronous reconciliation.** Playlist mutations return **`202`**, meaning *accepted into the desired queue*, not *on air*. Nothing changed until `appliedRevision` catches up with `desiredRevision`. A non-null `applyError` means the engine rejected it.

**3. Two-phase validation.** `POST /rundowns/{id}/apply` with `"dryRun": true` validates the merged result and rolls back. It is the safe way to test a schedule edit.

## Units

Every duration, offset and fade on the API is **integer milliseconds**. A graphic's duration is the whole visible interval, fades included.

## Variables

`{{baseUrl}}` comes from the **skandha-local** environment. `{{playlistId}}` and `{{rundownId}}` are collection variables, both `main`. Everything else is captured at runtime by the workflow scripts.

item.name: 01 Inputs

request.description:
Every logical input with its streams, URIs, states and current selection. For a playlist input, each entry in `streams` is one switchable playlist item.

Only `transcoder.inputs[0]` becomes an engine input — do not use `/config/get-inputs` to count them.

**Capture:** stores `inputId` and picks a `streamId` that is not currently on air.

One input. Poll this after a switch until `currentStreamId` matches what you asked for — the switch is asynchronous.

**Needs** `{{inputId}}`. Unknown id → `404`.

exec: pm.test("200, or 400/404 for a bad id", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 400, 404]));
if (pm.response.code === 200) console.log("switch requested - poll 'Get input' until currentStreamId matches");

request.description:
Point the input at a different stream. Asynchronous: poll `GET /inputs/{id}`.

**Needs** `{{inputId}}`, `{{streamId}}`. Missing `currentStreamId` → `400`; unknown id → `404`.

**Caveat:** on a managed playlist the reconciler may switch back. `POST /playlists/main/skip` is the supported way to change what is on air.

exec: pm.test("a local file reports a duration", () => pm.expect(p.durationSeconds).to.be.a("number"));

request.description:
Probe a clip under MEDIA_DIR. `uri` may be `file:///abs`, an absolute path, or a path relative to MEDIA_DIR; anything resolving outside MEDIA_DIR is rejected with 400.

A local file is the only case that reports `bitrateBps` reliably.

exec: pm.test("probed the first entry, not the manifest", () => pm.expect(p.probedUri).to.not.match(/\.m3u8$/));

query.description: pls+file:///runtime/main.m3u8 (the + must be percent-encoded in a query string)

request.description:
Probe the engine's playlist.

**This reports the playlist's FIRST ENTRY, not the M3U8.** The engine's playlist is a UTPL schedule — `#EXTINF:-1` lines followed by `file://` entries — and ffprobe returns `Invalid data found` if handed it directly, because it is a schedule and not a container. `probedUri` names the media file that was actually probed.

The M3U8 must live under `MEDIA_DIR` or `PLAYLIST_ROOT` (default `/runtime`); every entry inside it is confined to `MEDIA_DIR`. An entry pointing outside returns 400, an empty playlist returns 422.

Probe a live UDP source, for example `udp://239.1.1.1:5000`.

Add `interfaceAddress` to join a multicast group on a specific NIC — the equivalent of `transport.udp.multicast.interfaces`. Without it, a multicast probe can time out on a multi-homed appliance where the engine itself works.

`bitrateBps` is null for a live source: ffprobe reports no container bitrate for non-seekable input.

Probe an SRT listener by calling it, for example `srt://10.0.0.1:9000?mode=caller&latency=125`.

**Latency is milliseconds here**, matching `transport.srt.latency` in the engine configuration. libsrt itself wants microseconds, so the route converts and echoes the result in `probedUri` — check it reads `latency=125000`.

Use `mode=listener` to bind and wait for an encoder to call in instead; that defaults to a 20 second wait and sets `waitedForCaller`.

Probe an HLS manifest over http(s).

The ffprobe protocol whitelist for this transport deliberately excludes `file`, so a manifest listing `file://` segments cannot make the API read local files. Credentials in the userinfo are rejected rather than forwarded.
NDI is in the transport enum so it can be refused with an explanation rather than a validation error: ffmpeg has no NDI input protocol, so an NDI source cannot be probed at all.

item.description:
The engine's live inputs and their switchable streams. For a playlist input each entry in `streams` is one playlist item.

Only `transcoder.inputs[0]` becomes an engine input — do not use `/config/get-inputs` to count them.

item.name: 02 Media

request.description:
Every registered asset with its ffprobe output. `probe.format.duration` is the real clip length in seconds — the rundown needs it to project start times.

**Capture:** stores the first asset as `mediaId`.

formdata.description: Select a video file. Field name must stay 'file' and type must be File, not Text.

request.description:
Multipart upload. Writes a **fresh UUID-named copy** into `MEDIA_DIR`, so the asset it creates is yours alone and safe to delete afterwards.

**The form field must be named exactly `file`, and its type must be `File`, not `Text`.** A wrong name or an unreadable path both produce `400 Field required` — the server sees no file at all. Sending a valid `file` with a bad extension produces `422 unsupported media file extension` instead.

Allowed: `.avi .m2ts .m4v .mkv .mov .mp4 .mpeg .mpg .mxf .ts .webm`.

**Portability:** Postman stores a *local path*, not the file. Re-select it on another machine, and pass `--working-dir` to Newman.

exec: console.log("WARNING: import dedupes by path. This may be an EXISTING asset the channel depends on - do not Delete media on it.");

request.description:
Registers a file that is already inside `MEDIA_DIR`, by relative path. No upload, so this one is fully portable.

**⚠️ It dedupes by `relativePath`.** If the file is already registered you get back the **existing** asset, not a copy — so the id you receive may be one the live channel depends on. Never follow this with *Delete media* on a clip the channel uses.

exec: pm.test("204 deleted, or 409 while still queued", () =>
if (pm.response.code === 409) console.log("still referenced by a playlist item - dequeue it first");
if (pm.response.code === 204) console.log("asset and its file are gone from disk");

request.description:
**⚠️ Destructive — this unlinks the file from disk**, it does not merely deregister it.

`409` while a playlist item references the asset in a state other than `played`. That guard is incomplete: an asset referenced only by a `played` item deletes cleanly, taking the file with it. **Only delete assets you created via Upload.**

**Needs** `{{mediaId}}`. Success is `204` with no body.

item.description:
The media library. Registering a clip is separate from putting it in the queue.

**Allowed extensions:** `.avi .m2ts .m4v .mkv .mov .mp4 .mpeg .mpg .mxf .ts .webm`. Anything else → `422 unsupported media file extension`.

item.name: 03 Playlist

request.description:
The queue snapshot. The two revisions are the whole concurrency story:

- `desiredRevision == appliedRevision` → settled, safe to mutate
- `desiredRevision > appliedRevision` → reconciliation in flight
- `applyError` non-null → the engine rejected the desired queue

`currentItemId` is the item on air.

**Capture:** stores `expectedRevision`, and an `itemId` that is *not* on air.

exec: pm.test("202 accepted (not on air yet)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(202));
console.log(`desired ${s.desiredRevision}, applied ${s.appliedRevision} - re-send 'Get playlist' until they match`);

request.description:
Adds a registered asset to the queue. Omit `position` to append; `position` is 0-based from the front.

**Returns `202`** — accepted into the *desired* queue, not on air. Poll *Get playlist* until `appliedRevision` catches up.

**⚠️ While the rundown service is enabled this does not stick.** The reconciler removes the item about a second later because it is not in the active rundown version. Use `POST /rundowns/main/apply` with `insertItems` instead — see **W1**.

`expectedRevision` is an unquoted integer; quoting it gives `422`. A stale value gives `409`.

exec: pm.test("202, or 409 if stale or on air", () =>

request.description:
Moves an item to a new 0-based position.

`409` if the revision is stale **or the item is on air**. `503 cannot confirm the on-air item` if the engine is not answering — a retry loop that only handles `409` will still fall over.

**⚠️ While the rundown service is enabled, the reconciler re-projects the active version and undoes this.** Reorder programs by applying a rundown document with the items in the order you want.

exec: pm.test("202, or 409 if on air / stale", () =>

request.description:
Removes an item from the desired queue. `expectedRevision` goes in the **query string** here, not the body.

`409 cannot delete the item on air; use skip`. `503` if the engine cannot confirm what is on air.

**⚠️ While the rundown service is enabled, use `removeItem` via `POST /rundowns/main/apply` instead.** Removing here leaves the rundown version unchanged, so the next projection puts the item straight back.

Cuts immediately to the next item.

The only queue write that is **not** reconciled and carries no revision — which is why it is the supported way to change what is on air, and the escape hatch when a `409` says an item cannot be touched while playing.

Documents a deliberate removal: managed playlists run continuously, so Start and Pause are gone.

Returns **`410`** with `managed playlists run continuously; Start and Pause are unavailable`. Kept in the collection so the behaviour is discoverable instead of surprising. `pause` behaves identically.

item.description:
The managed on-air queue. It loops continuously.

**⚠️ While `ENABLE_RUNDOWN_SERVICE=true`, the rundown owns this queue.** A direct Insert, Reorder or Remove here is accepted with `202` and then **reverted within about a second**: the reconciler deletes any playlist item that is not in the active rundown version, logging `on_air_bridge_removed`. Verified on this container 2026-08-21.

So these routes are the right ones only when scheduling is **off**. With it on, change the schedule through `POST /rundowns/main/apply` (`insertItems`, `removeItem`) — see **W1**.

`POST /skip` is the exception: it is immediate, unreconciled, and works either way.

Every other mutation here is **reconciled, not immediate** — read `desiredRevision` before you write, and poll until `appliedRevision` matches.

item.name: 04 Graphics

exec: const safe = assets.find(a => (a.kind === "logo" || a.kind === "bug") && a.enabled !== false);

request.description:
Available assets with `kind`, `mediaType`, `defaultMode`, `defaultAnimationMs` and `preloadLeadMs`.

Video assets are returned with `enabled: false` while `ENABLE_VIDEO_GRAPHICS=false` — the Compose default, and not a fault.

**Capture:** stores a non-squeeze `graphicAssetId` and its `graphicMode`.

exec: if (squeeze.length) console.log(`squeeze lock HELD by ${squeeze.map(c => c.kind).join(", ")}`);

request.description:
Cues currently scheduled, on air, or restoring.

`phase` moves `scheduled → on_air → restoring`, then the cue disappears from this list entirely. An L-band or Aston cue in **any** of those phases holds the shared squeeze lock and blocks the other.

Fires a graphic. All times are milliseconds; `durationMs` is the **whole visible interval**, fades included.

- `durationMs: null` holds indefinitely (logo and bug only)
- `startInMs: 0` starts immediately
- for a **video** asset, `startInMs` must be at least the asset's `preloadLeadMs` (3000 by default)

Rejected if an L-band or Aston cue already holds the squeeze lock. The same pair inside one `POST /rundowns/main/apply` is accepted — batching is what decides whether it works.

Cancels a cue early and runs its restoration. `204` with no body.

A `404` means the cue already finished on its own — not an error.

**Needs** `{{cueId}}`.

item.description:
Manual graphics cues — logo, bug, L-band and Aston sponsors.

**L-band and Aston share a backend squeeze lock.** Two separate cues over the same window are refused; the same pair inside one `POST /rundowns/main/apply` is accepted.

item.name: 05 SSAI · Scheduled events

query.description: ISO 8601. Lower bound on event time.
ISO 8601. Upper bound on event time.

request.description:
All scheduled events, newest first. The four optional filters are disabled by default — enable them in the **Params** tab.

The list mixes SCTE-35 ad signalling with the graphics overlay events the rundown dispatches, so expect more than just your ad breaks.

**Capture:** stores the newest event as `eventId`.

exec: console.log("cue out sent - remember to send a matching cue in (type 53, same segmentation_event_id)");

request.description:
Opens an ad break.

Three things worth knowing about this body:

- it is a **bare JSON array**, not an object
- `segmentation_type_id: 52` (0x34) is **Provider Placement Opportunity Start**, from SCTE 35 Table 23 — the full table is at `doc/codebase/38-scte35-segmentation-type-id-table.md`. The matching end id `53` is **rejected here with 400**: a time_signal break closes on its `segmentation_duration`, never on a manual cue-in
- `segmentation_duration` is in **90 kHz ticks** — 30 s × 90000 = 2700000. It is the one duration on this API that is not milliseconds

`time: null` fires immediately; otherwise supply an ISO 8601 timestamp up to 14 days ahead. Keep `segmentation_event_id` — the matching cue in must reuse it.

The splice-insert variant uses `type: "scte35_spliceinsert"` with `{duration, splice_event_id}`, where `duration` **is** milliseconds. Use **W6** for the full break.

Removes one event by its **integer** id — not a UUID, unlike most ids on this API.

**Needs** `{{eventId}}`. Run *List scheduled events* first to capture one.

item.description:
SCTE-35 ad signalling and other scheduled events.

The POST body is a **bare JSON array** of events, not an object. `time` may be `null` for immediate execution, or an ISO 8601 timestamp up to 14 days ahead.

An ad break is **two** events — cue out and cue in. Nothing pairs them server-side; tracking the break is the caller's job.

item.name: 06 Rundown

request.description:
Is scheduling switched on? The one rundown route that stays reachable while the service is disabled, so an operator can always discover why the workspace is unavailable.

`bootstrapState` reports the declarative channel file: `unchanged` after a restart that changed nothing. `enabled: false` means every other route in this folder returns `404`.

What is live, plus the publish history. **Normally your first request** — copy `activeVersionId` and read the document next.

`versions[]` is a history of what has been **broadcast**, not of keystrokes: every row in it was on air at some point.

**Capture:** stores `versionId`.

The complete schedule: programs, their graphics, stable IDs, durations and timeline positions.

`items[].stableItemId` is the join key to the playlist — it equals `PlaylistItem.id` in `GET /playlists/main`. `items[].key` is what `ops` address.

`timelineDurationMs` is the loop length. `scheduledGraphics[]` holds wall-clock graphics tied to no program.

**Needs** `{{versionId}}` — run *Get rundown* first.

What is on air right now, and when this schedule synced. The anchor the operator grid projects row start times from.

- `currentStartedAt` is **observed fact**; every other row's time is projected from it
- `cycle` counts completed loops since `syncedAt`
- `serverNow` lets a browser correct for clock skew — without it every projected time is wrong by the container/browser difference

Timing comes from 250 ms control-plane polling, not timecode. Nulls are legitimate when nothing has aired yet.

Validates the change and **rolls back**. Nothing reaches air; `version` comes back `null` while `applied` still reports what would have happened.

This is the safe way to test an edit, and it is what the operator page's YAML import preview uses.

**The five operations:** `addGraphic`, `updateGraphic`, `removeGraphic`, `removeItem`, `insertItems`. `addGraphic` needs **exactly one** of `itemKey` (item-relative) or `startsAt` (wall-clock).

Supply exactly one of `ops` or `document` — both, or neither, is `422`.

exec: if (f.state === "failed") console.log(`ON AIR but ${f.path} not rewritten (${f.error}) - lost on restart`);

request.description:
The single write path. Reads the live version, applies the ops to a copy, validates the **result**, and publishes it in one transaction — either the whole change reaches air or nothing moves.

`409` if `expectedVersionId` is stale. Pass `null` to force the change through regardless.

Apply also rewrites the declarative channel file and reports the outcome in `channelFile`, so an applied change survives a restart.

Two validation rules bite here: a graphic must fit inside its clip **including 1200 ms of restoration**, and L-band and Aston may not share a squeeze window.

The alternative to `ops`: send the complete end state. A client that already holds the whole document — as the operator grid does, because it edits a copy — should not have to synthesise the operations that would produce it. Both paths share one validation.

Paste a document from *Get version document* into `document` before sending. The empty `{}` here is deliberate: the service layer rejects it, which is what you want to see once.

**Presence, not truthiness** — sending `document: {}` alongside `ops` is still "both", and returns `422`.

exec: console.log(r.version ? `committed as version ${r.version.number}` : "dry run - nothing published");

formdata.description: A channel YAML, max 1 MiB, UTF-8.

request.description:
Splices a channel YAML's programs into the live schedule.

**It imports a program *list*, not the media.** Upload the clips with `POST /media` first, or you get `422` naming the unregistered path.

Other `422`s: wrong `channel:`, bare durations without units, over 1 MiB, non-UTF-8.

Preview with `dryRun=true`, then send again with `false` to commit — that two-step is what the operator page's import preview does.

**Portability:** the file is a local path. Not runnable in CI without `--working-dir`.

Publishes a first version from the playlist that is already running.

`apply` edits the *live* version, so a channel that has never published one has no way in — this is it. Returns `201`.

**Only for a fresh channel.** On `main`, which already has a live version, expect this to be unnecessary. The operator page calls it exactly once: when `GET /rundowns/main` returns `404`.

Turns a local date and time into a UTC instant **in the rundown's timezone**, and tells you which offset it used.

A date and time typed by a human is not a valid instant until something resolves it — DST and the channel timezone both matter. Resolve first, then put `startsAt` into an `addGraphic` op with a wall-clock trigger.

`date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD`; `time` is `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`.

As-run history: every observed program transition, newest first, **capped at 200** — roughly 40 minutes at a 37 s loop.

`observedAt` is written by the 250 ms poller at each transition; `endedAt` is null for the item still on air. This is the only real timing record in the system — `PlaylistItem.started_at` is a dead column nothing writes.

Use `GET /clock` instead if you only need "what is on now"; it is one small object rather than 200 rows.

exec: pm.test("no failed executions", () => pm.expect(failed.length, failed.map(f => f.error).join("; ")).to.eql(0));

request.description:
**Did a graphic actually fire?** `apply` tells you a graphic is *scheduled*; only this tells you it aired.

`state` is `pending`, `dispatched` or `error`; `cueId` links to the graphics cue that was created. `error` carries the reason when the dispatch failed.

Newest first, capped at 200. The operator grid polls this every 3 s to badge each graphic.

Who changed what. One row per action — publish, import, seed — with the subject and a `details` object, newest first, capped at 200.

Useful after an unexpected schedule change: the audit log says which action produced the version that is live.

item.description:
The versioned schedule — programs plus their graphics triggers.

**There is one kind of stored object: a version.** Every version in the history was on air at some point; there is no draft. A change is either live or it is unsaved text in your client.

The usual path is `Get rundown` → `Get version document` → `Apply ops`. `dryRun: true` checks a change before committing to it.

Available only while `ENABLE_RUNDOWN_SERVICE=true`; otherwise every route here except `/status` returns `404`.

item.name: 07 Engine config

exec: // Seeds the round-trip PUT below, so replacing the config writes back exactly
// what is already live rather than something invented here.

request.description:
The whole engine config as JSON, read from the path in `TRANSCODER_CONFIG_PATH` (default `/opt/utpl/etc/config.json`).

Read-only and safe. The test stores the document in the `configDocument` collection variable, which **Validate** and **Replace** below send back unchanged — run this one first.

`GET /config/get-config` is the original spelling and still works.
The `transcoder.outputs` array. The supplied contract is fixed H.264 1920×1080 at 25 fps, regardless of the source resolution or frame rate of the playlist files.

One output by **0-based array index**, not an id.

An out-of-range index returns `{"message": "output_id doesn't exist"}` with HTTP **200**, not a `404` — so check the body, not the status.

exec: if (n > 1) console.log(`config lists ${n} inputs but only inputs[0] becomes an engine input`);

request.description:
⚠️ **Misleading — do not use this to count engine inputs.**

It returns the `transcoder.inputs` array *from the config file*. Only `transcoder.inputs[0]` ever becomes a real engine input, so this list can be longer than reality.

Use `GET /inputs` (folder 01) for what the engine actually has.
One configured input by 0-based index. Same caveat as *Get inputs*: this is the config file, not the engine. Out of range returns a `message` body with HTTP 200.

Asks Supervisor for the engine process state. `{"message": "RUNNING"}` is healthy.

`500` means the API could not reach the Supervisor socket — a permissions or path problem, not necessarily a dead engine.

Poll this after a restart until it reads `RUNNING`.

Runs validation and the writability probe, then stops. **Nothing is written.**

The safe way to check a document before committing to it. Send any candidate config as the body; this sends back whatever **Get config** last read.

exec: pm.test("written, and a restart is needed", () => {
console.log(`wrote ${b.path} - restart the engine to pick it up`);

request.description:
⚠️ **Writes the config file.**

Replaces the whole document. As sent here it is a round trip — the body is the `configDocument` variable that **Get config** stored, so it writes back what is already live and changes nothing. Edit the body to actually change the channel.

The engine parses its config once at start, so this takes effect only after **Restart transcoder** below; that is what `restartRequired` in the response means.

The write is validated first and then applied as an atomic rename, so a rejected document leaves the previous file untouched.

item.name: Replace config — rejects an object where an array belongs

request.description:
The failure the retired setters used to write silently: `outputs` as an object rather than an array. Valid JSON, invalid config — the engine would have failed to start with nothing pointing back at the write.

Expect **422** and an unchanged file. Run **Get config** afterwards to confirm nothing moved.

item.name: Replace config — rejects a JSON array body

request.description:
The body must be the config **object**. An array is refused by request validation before any of the write path runs.

Expect **400**.

⚠️ **Takes the channel off air for the duration of the restart.**

Stops the engine when it is running, waits `TRANSCODER_RESTART_GRACE_SECONDS` (default 10), and starts it. An engine in any other state is started without a stop.

This is how a `PUT /config` takes effect. `GET` on the same path still works but is deprecated — it changes state, so it should not be a GET.

Allow ~15 s before the stream returns.

**Retired.** Returns `410` naming `PUT /config`.

This route never wrote anything: it called `json.loads()` on a body FastAPI had already parsed, raised `TypeError` into a bare `except:`, and answered **HTTP 200** — so a caller checking only the status code believed the write had succeeded.

It also reached only `transcoder.inputs` and `transcoder.outputs`, leaving `version`, `squeeze`, `scte`, `blanking`, `blackout` and the whole `application` object unaddressable. `PUT /config` replaces all four routes and covers the rest of the document.

item.description:
Engine configuration and process control.

**⚠️ All four setters are broken and cannot write.** `set-outputs`, `set-output`, `set-inputs` and `set-input` each call `json.loads()` on a body FastAPI has already parsed into a dict, raise `TypeError`, swallow it in a bare `except:`, and return `{"message": "error parsing request"}` with HTTP **200**. Verified against this container on 2026-08-21.

The project docs flag only `set-input`/`set-inputs`; the output setters fail identically. Configure the engine before starting the container.

The getters are fine and read-only. `restart-transcoder` works and **interrupts the live output**.

item.name: 08 Licence
item.description:
The engine license on this appliance — the channel UI's **Licence** tab.

The engine reads its license once, at start, so **upload restarts the engine and delete stops it**; both take the channel off air. Every check is done by the engine binary itself (`--license-info`), because the keys that decrypt a license exist only inside it.

Issuing licenses (generate, sign, list) is not here: it needs the signing private key, which stays on the vendor side. Use `transcoder/license/make-license.sh`.

request.description:
The installed engine license as the engine binary reads it (`transcoder -l <file> --license-info`): `status` (`valid`, `expired`, `notYetValid`, or `invalid` with `error`), `name`, `id`, `validSince`/`validUntil` (ms since epoch), `ttl` (ms), `offline`, `maxSessions`, `createdAt`, `checkedAt`, and `path` (`TRANSCODER_LICENSE_PATH`).

Read-only and safe. An installed file the engine would refuse is still described with **200** so you can see why. **404** means no license is installed; **503** means the engine binary could not be asked.

Checks an uploaded license with the engine binary **without installing it or touching the engine**. Returns `state: "validated"` and the engine's report as `license`.

**422** with `license refused: …` when the engine would not start on it: corrupted or not a license, signed with the other key set (a development license on a production build), expired, not yet valid, or an online license while the engine config has no `application.licenseServer.uri` beginning `http://`/`https://`. Also 422 for an empty file or one over 64 KiB.

**The form field must be named exactly `file`, and its type must be `File`, not `Text`.** Postman stores a local path, not the file; re-select it on another machine.

request.description:
**Takes the channel off air.** Validates the upload exactly as the dry run does; a refused file (422) leaves the installed license and the engine untouched. An accepted file replaces the installed license atomically, then the engine is **restarted** on it — off air for `TRANSCODER_RESTART_GRACE_SECONDS` (default 10 s) plus engine start-up.

Returns `state: "installed"`, the report as `license`, and the Supervisor state as `engine`. If the restart itself fails the license stays installed and the error says so; retry with `POST /config/restart-transcoder`.

**409** when the license directory is missing or not writable, or the license is bind-mounted as a single file — it must sit inside a read-write mounted directory.

request.description:
**Takes the channel off air until a new license is uploaded.** Stops the engine, then removes the installed license, and returns `state: "removed"` with `engine: "STOPPED"`. The engine cannot start without a license: `POST /config/start-transcoder` will report `STARTING` and the engine then exits, leaving Supervisor in `BACKOFF`/`FATAL`. Recover with **Upload licence**.

**404** with no license installed, and the engine is not stopped. If the stop fails (500) the license stays in place. In the Compose profile a deleted license stays deleted across container restarts.

request.description:
CPU, memory, storage, storage writes and network, for the container (API + engine), the engine process alone, and the host. Read-only and safe to poll.

The figures come from a background sampler (every `STATS_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 2 s), so the response is immediate and rates are over `windowSeconds`. Right after the API starts, rates are null until the second sample.

**Units:** CPU in cores and percent of the container's CPU capacity; memory and storage in bytes; storage writes in bytes per second; network in **bits** per second.

**Storage writes** are given twice: `engine` is what the transcoder writes, `container` is what reaches the disk. The kernel flushes to disk in bursts up to ~30 s later, so use `averageBytesPerSecond` (last 60 s) rather than the 2 s `bytesPerSecond` for a steady figure.
